newsitem.title: USA: WCI Steel gets Renco acquisition offer.
newsitem.headline: WCI Steel gets Renco acquisition offer.

text.p: WCI Steel Inc said on Thursday Renco Group Inc has offered to acquire all of the WCI shares it does not already own for $10 a share cash.
Renco's proposal to the board would take the company private, said WCI, which is 84 percent owned by Renco.
The tender offer would be conditioned upon sufficient shares being tendered so that WCI Holdings would own at least 90 percent of WCI's common stock, WCI said.
Public WCI shareholders who do not tender their shares would receive in the merger the same price of $10 per share in a "short form" merger after the 90 percent threshold was met, WCI said.

Renco also proposes that WCI commence an offer to purchase all, but not less than a majority, of WCI's outstanding 10-1/2 Senior Notes due 2002 (currently approximately $206 million) at a purchase price of 111.5 percent of principal, WCI said.
Renco also proposes that WCI simultaneously offer $300 million of new senior notes.

WCI said proceeds from the new notes, which would be privately placed, and the company's available cash would be used to pay for the transactions and related expenses, pay a dividend to Renco and cover contractual payments to certain WCI executives.
The "going private" transaction and the debt tender and refinancing transaction would each be contingent upon the success of the other, the company said.
WCI's independent directors will assess the fairness of Renco's offer, WCI said.
